assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cărtărescu's visionary, densely patterned prose has an unusually strong claim on distinctiveness of voice and imaginative ambition. Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid build a metaphysical project from the body, memory and the Bucharest of his childhood. The long sentences and hallucinatory architecture are a real formal achievement. The ambition is sustained across volumes and also across his poetry and essays. His work connects European modernist and visionary traditions to a specifically Romanian post-communist experience.
assessment.attribution: A single named writer with a clear, recognizable contribution: the expansive, oneiric Romanian novel of consciousness. The proposed citation would centre on the large-scale fiction. The poetry and essays would be secondary.
assessment.maturity: A long, consistent career with major works from the 1980s onward and a late-career cycle (Solenoid) that extends the project instead of repeating it. The oeuvre appears durable and ready for consideration.
uncertainties: Judgment of the prose rests heavily on translation, and the rhythm and syntactic density of the Romanian original may be only partly conveyed.
Coverage of the poetry and the early work is uneven in translation.
The scale and recurring motifs of the late novels may divide readers on whether they sustain their length.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Carson has an unmistakable voice and has remade genre boundaries among classical scholarship, lyric, verse novel, essay and visual form. Autobiography of Red recasts the Geryon myth as a contemporary verse novel. Nox is an object-like elegy for her brother. Her translations and reworkings of Greek material are also part of the achievement. Her formal intelligence and intellectual depth are high, and the line-level quality is consistently strong.
assessment.attribution: Clearly one writer with a distinct hybrid practice. A citation would need to cover poetry, essay and translation-inflected work together instead of a single genre.
assessment.maturity: Decades of sustained production with a stable reputation among poets and critics. The corpus is relatively compact and varied in form, which makes uniform depth harder to assess than for a large novelistic oeuvre.
uncertainties: Much of the work is in the form of books and performance pieces whose visual and material aspects may not carry across editions.
Her relation to Nobel's 'idealistic direction' is open to interpretation.
I have not independently verified the latest publications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Tawada makes linguistic estrangement a literary method by writing in both Japanese and German. The Emissary and Memoirs of a Polar Bear show a precise, playful intelligence, with fable, dystopia and language-play combined. Her work in fiction, poetry, essay and theatre shows breadth, and her formal inventiveness is of high quality. She is a significant case of literature beyond a single national language.
assessment.attribution: One writer with a clear and original contribution at the intersection of two literary languages. The citation would be easy to frame, though it must acknowledge two bodies of work.
assessment.maturity: A long career with consistent invention and growing international attention. The body of work is deep, though some of it is short and fable-like, which affects how monumental it seems.
uncertainties: Her bilingual play depends on features of Japanese and German that are partly lost in English translation.
Her German-language work is only partly available to me in translation.
The poetry and drama are less well covered than the novels.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Zurita turns the trauma of the Chilean dictatorship and the Latin American landscape into poetry of collective memory. Purgatory and Anteparadise combine personal wound, Dantean structure and landscape-scale interventions. The scale and moral seriousness of the vision are exceptional, and the poetry has a distinctive voice. It is a significant renewal of the modern lyric as public memorial.
assessment.attribution: One poet, with a well-defined contribution in the poetic sequence and in extra-textual works. The citation would centre on the poetry.
assessment.maturity: A career of more than four decades from the late 1970s, with continued development. The core works are well established and the body of work is coherent.
uncertainties: Poetry travels badly in translation, and my sense of the formal achievement relies on partial English versions.
The landscape and sky-writing interventions are hard to judge as literature on the page.
Later work may vary in intensity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Can Xue writes dreamlike, uncanny fiction that destabilizes psychology, space and causality, which gives it a strong claim to distinctiveness of voice. Frontier and Love in the New Millennium extend a radical experimental line in Chinese fiction, drawing on Kafka, Borges and her own idiom. Her intellectual seriousness is clear in her criticism and in her sustained commitment to the method.
assessment.attribution: One writer with a clear, singular contribution. The citation would centre on formal experiment in fiction and might include her literary criticism.
assessment.maturity: Decades of consistent production since the 1980s. The method is stable, which supports coherence but raises the question of how far it develops over time.
uncertainties: Translation is by a small number of translators, and the prose style is hard to judge from English.
Because the method recurs, the variety and range of the oeuvre are uncertain.
Only a fraction of her large output has been translated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wright's large, polyphonic novels, Carpentaria and The Swan Book among them, bring Indigenous sovereignty, oral storytelling and ecological time into the novel in an original English. The scale, formal ambition and moral force are substantial. The work is significant not for its subject alone but for its narrative construction and its remaking of the novel's forms.
assessment.attribution: One writer with a clear contribution. The citation would address the novels and the collective-memoir and nonfiction work as part of the same project.
assessment.maturity: The number of major novels is relatively small, so sustained quality over a long career is harder to assess than for some others. Recent work suggests continuing development.
uncertainties: The oeuvre is smaller than that of several other candidates.
I cannot verify how well the oral-form effects hold up in different editions and translations.
Her most recent works are not covered in this packet.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Michon's dense, compressed prose transforms obscure lives and art history into narrative inquiry of great stylistic intensity. Small Lives and The Eleven show an exacting command of French sentence rhythm and a serious meditation on art, power and the transmission of lives. The quality is very high on a small scale.
assessment.attribution: One writer with an unmistakable and well-defined contribution. A citation would centre on the short, intense prose narratives.
assessment.maturity: A relatively slim body of work, produced slowly since the 1980s. The quality is consistent, but breadth is limited compared with larger oeuvres.
uncertainties: The French style is highly compressed and may be only partly accessible in translation.
The narrow output makes the case for 'significance across the body of work' harder to demonstrate.
Only part of the oeuvre is available in English.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adonis remade modern Arabic poetic language through myth, fragmentation and a long critical dialogue with classical forms. Songs of Mihyar the Damascene and A Time Between Ashes and Roses are central to that project. His poetic and critical work on the Arabic tradition is intellectually weighty, and his influence on modern Arabic poetry is considerable.
assessment.attribution: One writer, with a well-defined contribution in both poetry and criticism. The citation would centre on the renewal of Arabic poetry.
assessment.maturity: A career of many decades with a major, established place in Arabic letters. The late-career work is less central to the argument for the oeuvre.
uncertainties: Arabic poetry is especially hard to judge in translation, particularly its prosody and its dialogue with classical forms.
Cultural and political prominence must not be confused with literary merit.
I cannot verify the quality of the full body of translation.
